answer.rationale: memory_73 (promotional pricing) scores lowest for sustainable long-term qualified revenue because price-based acquisition typically attracts price-sensitive cohorts with lower lifetime value, higher churn risk, and weaker unit economics—the record notes 'acquisition and revenue lift' but omits retention, cohort quality, or margin data critical to sustainability. memory_44 (sales-assisted enterprise) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding) score highest: enterprise sales-assisted flows directly correlate with higher contract values and retention, and shortened onboarding directly improves time-to-value and reduces early churn, both foundational to sustainable revenue. memory_31 (signup simplification for SMB activation) and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) score 4 each: they improve early engagement and reduce friction, but the record does not address cohort retention or unit economics post-activation. memory_57 (referral incentives) scores 3: it adds revenue from established customers with presumably better retention profiles, but the note explicitly acknowledges only 'no measurable harm to retention' rather than demonstrating net positive sustainability impact.
